title: Mangalyaan: Mars on the First Try

endcard.line: Pictures: ISRO Mars Orbiter Mission data, processed by Justin Cowart (CC BY 2.0); 4-RAZOR 01 (CC0)

segments.say: Many of the world's first missions to Mars failed. India's reached Mars orbit on its very first try.
The Mars Orbiter Mission, Mangalyaan, launched on the fifth of November, twenty thirteen. On the twenty-fourth of September, twenty fourteen, it slipped into orbit around Mars.

anim.title: Firsts
items: First Asian country to reach Mars orbit
First country to do it on the first attempt

segments.say: That made India the first Asian country to reach Mars orbit, and the first in the world to do it on the first attempt.
The whole mission cost about four hundred and fifty crore rupees, famously less than some Hollywood space films.
Its colour camera sent back full-disc pictures of Mars, its volcanoes and its dust storms.
It was built to last six months. It kept working for about eight years, until contact was lost in twenty twenty-two.
For GS Three: Mangalyaan showed that a careful, low-cost design could reach Mars, first time.

sources: ISRO, Mars Orbiter Mission page: launched 5 November 2013 on PSLV-C25; Mars orbit insertion 24 September 2014; India first to reach Mars orbit on the first attempt
PIB, 24 September 2014 and Lok Sabha answers: mission cost about ₹450 crore
ISRO / national committee statement, October 2022: ground contact with the spacecraft lost; mission had far outlived its designed six-month life

quiz.q: When did Mangalyaan enter Mars orbit?
quiz.why: Launch was November 2013; Mars orbit came on 24 September 2014.

quiz.q: What was special about India's Mars mission?
options: It reached Mars orbit on the first attempt
It went to Jupiter after Mars
quiz.why: India was the first to reach Mars orbit on its first try.

quiz.q: How long was it designed to last?
quiz.why: It was built for six months and lasted about eight years.

reviewNote: Facts were read against ISRO's MOM page, PIB and the 2022 statement on loss of contact. Mars pictures are ISRO data processed by an amateur (CC BY 2.0); the model photo is CC0. Moving facts: none.
